## Decisions already made by the maintainer

<content>
1: # opencode-readonly-guard
2: 
3: Make opencode's read-only agents (`plan`, `explore`, and any agent with `edit: deny`) actually read-only.
4: 
5: In opencode, "plan mode" is a request to the model, not a restriction: the `plan` and `explore` agents can run any
6: shell command, so a model that ignores the reminder can still `rm`, `sed -i` or `> file`. This plugin closes that gap:
7: 
8: - **Write guard.** Before opencode evaluates any permission rule, the full command line is parsed and refused if it
9:   writes: redirections in any position, `tee` to a file, `rm`/`cp`/`mv`/…, `sed -i`, `git commit`, `npm install`,
10:   `find -delete`, `curl -o`, and wrappers around them (`sudo`, `env`, `xargs`, `bash -c`, `$(…)`). The model gets an
11:   error that tells it to return the data in its reply instead.
12: - **Shared allowlist.** Read-only agents ask before running anything except a vetted list of read-only commands
13:   (`ls`, `cat`, `rg`, `git log`, `herdr agent list`, …). The list lives in [`rules/`](rules) as plain JSON that anyone
14:   can extend.
15: - **Reviewed learning.** An "always" answer in a read-only agent is only logged as a candidate. `/guard-review` shows
16:   candidates with safe pattern options, and a rule is added only after you confirm the exact pattern.
17: - **Event log.** Every shell command, block, prompt and answer in a read-only agent is recorded, so the policy can be
18:   improved with data.
19: 
20: Tested with opencode 1.19.3 (supported range `>=1.18.29 <2`). opencode 2.x has a different plugin API and is not
21: supported yet, see [TODO.md](TODO.md).
22: 
23: ## Install
24: 
25: ```sh
26: opencode plugin opencode-readonly-guard --global   # adds it to ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
27: ```
28: 
29: or add it to your config by hand, with options if you want them:
30: 
31: ```jsonc
32: // opencode.json
33: {
34:   "plugin": [
35:     "opencode-readonly-guard",
36:     // or: ["opencode-readonly-guard", { "agents": { "include": ["reviewer"] }, "allow": ["whoami *"] }]
37:   ],
38: }
39: ```
40: 
41: Restart opencode afterwards (config and plugins are loaded once at startup).
42: 
43: Other ways:
44: 
45: | Tool        | Command                                                                           |
46: | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
47: | npm / bun   | `npm i -g opencode-readonly-guard` · `bun add -g opencode-readonly-guard`         |
48: | mise (CLI)  | `mise use -g npm:opencode-readonly-guard`                                         |
49: | From source | `git clone … && mise run setup build`, then `"plugin": ["file:///path/to/clone"]` |
50: 
51: > The package is not published to npm yet (see [TODO.md](TODO.md)). Until then, use the from-source route.
52: 
53: Load it once (not from both a global and a project config): two copies would both inject rules, register the same
54: tools and log every event twice.
55: 
56: ## Using it
57: 
58: **`/guard-review`** (registered by the plugin, runs in `build`) summarizes the log: blocked commands, the most-prompted
59: commands and allowlist candidates. For each candidate you pick the exact rule to keep (the exact command, the same
60: command limited to its directory, or opencode's general pattern, whichever the safety check accepts) or dismiss it.
61: opencode then asks you to confirm that exact pattern before it is written to `readonly-guard.json`. New rules apply
62: after a restart. In read-only agents the review tools are hidden, so an agent cannot extend its own allowlist.
63: 
64: **Command-line tool** (`opencode-readonly-guard`, also available as `npx opencode-readonly-guard`):
65: 
66: ```text
67: check [--json] [--no-store] <command>   what a read-only agent gets: allow | ask | block (exit status 0 | 1 | 2)
68: vet <pattern>                           may this pattern be added to the allowlist?
69: rules [--json]                          print the shared allowlist and the always-ask flags
70: review [--limit N]                      print the log summary
71: install [-g] [--force]                  opencode plugin opencode-readonly-guard
72: ```
73: 
74: ```console
75: $ opencode-readonly-guard check 'git log --oneline | head'
76: allow
77: $ opencode-readonly-guard check 'ls | cat > notes.txt'
78: block  write redirection "> notes.txt"
79: $ opencode-readonly-guard check 'whoami'
80: ask    needs approval: whoami
81: ```
82: 
83: ## How the policy is built
84: 
85: For every read-only agent the plugin writes this ordered bash rule list into the config (the last matching rule wins):
86: 
87: 1. `"*": ask`
88: 2. the shared allowlist, [`rules/allow.json`](rules/allow.json)
89: 3. presets that are on (see [Working inside herdr](#working-inside-herdr)), learned rules (`readonly-guard.json`) and
90:    the `allow` option, each re-checked at startup
91: 4. the agent's own bash rules, if it had any
92: 5. the always-ask flags, [`rules/ask.json`](rules/ask.json): `find -delete/-exec`, `rg --pre`, `git … --output`, …
93: 
94: Because the flags come last, a broad learned rule such as `find *` never silences `find . -delete`.
95: 
96: Read-only agents are `plan`, `explore`, every agent whose `permission.edit` is `deny` (or `tools.edit: false`), plus
97: `agents.include`, minus `agents.exclude`. `plan` additionally asks before delegating to a subagent that is not
98: read-only, and never to `general`.
99: 
100: ## Working inside herdr
101: 
102: Agents that run in a [herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane can inspect it with the `herdr` CLI. The rules treat `herdr` like
103: `git`: they judge the subcommand, never the program as a whole (`herdr *` is never accepted).
104: 
105: - **Allowed without a prompt:** `--help`, `--version`, `--skill`, a bare command group (`herdr agent`, `herdr pane`, …)
106:   and the read-only subcommands: `status`, `agent list|get|read|wait|explain`,
107:   `pane list|current|get|layout|process-info|neighbor|edges|read|wait-output`, `workspace|tab list|get`,
108:   `worktree|session|machine|plugin|integration` listings, `api snapshot|schema`, `config check`, `channel show`.
109: - **Always asks**, even when an agent's own rules allow `herdr *`, and can never be learned (exact or with a wildcard):
110:   every other subcommand, such as `pane send-text|send-keys|run|split|close`, `agent prompt|send-keys|start`,
111:   `tab|workspace create|close|focus`, `server stop`, `session stop`. A read-only agent must not send instructions to
112:   another agent, so `agent prompt` stays a prompt. The `--machine`, `--session` and `--remote` prefixes, bare `herdr`
113:   (it opens the terminal UI) and `--trust-repository` ask too.
114: - **Blocked** like other writes: `herdr update`, `worktree create|remove`, `config reset-keys`,
115:   `integration install|uninstall`, `session delete`, `plugin install|update`, `api schema --output FILE`, and
116:   `pane run PANE CMD` when `CMD` would itself be blocked (`herdr pane run w1:p2 'rm -rf build'`).
117: - **UI commands, on inside herdr:** `herdr tab rename` and `herdr notification show` only change what herdr
118:   displays, which is how a plan-mode agent can report its state. They are the `herdr-ui` preset: allowed without a
119:   prompt when opencode runs in a herdr pane (`HERDR_ENV=1`), and not otherwise. Outside a pane the herdr CLI still
120:   reaches the running session and acts on whatever is focused there, so a UI command listed in your store or options
121:   is ignored outside herdr too. The preset is built into the plugin and is not part of the shared allowlist.
122: 
123:   Switch it off with `"presets": { "herdr-ui": false }`, and list the one command you want instead:
124: 
125:   ```jsonc
126:   // ~/.config/opencode/readonly-guard.json (the store), or in the plugin options,
127:   // or in herdr's own directory: ~/.config/herdr/readonly-guard.json
128:   { "presets": { "herdr-ui": false }, "allow": ["herdr tab rename *"] }
129:   ```
130: 
131:   Where the settings come from:
132: 
133:   | Source                                  | Keys                    | Notes                                                       |
134:   | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
135:   | plugin options in `opencode.json`       | `presets`, `allow`      | lowest precedence                                           |
136:   | the store `readonly-guard.json`         | `presets`, `allow`, ... | the file `/guard-review` writes                             |
137:   | `readonly-guard.json` in herdr's config | `presets`, `allow`      | read only inside herdr, never written, wins over the others |
138: 
139:   herdr's directory is the one holding `$HERDR_CONFIG_PATH`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/herdr` (`~/.config/herdr`). If
140:   sources disagree about a preset, the last in the table wins; `allow` lists add up. Every `allow` pattern passes the
141:   same safety check, so no file can allow `herdr agent prompt`, and herdr's file may only hold `herdr …` patterns.
142:   `opencode-readonly-guard vet 'herdr tab rename *'` shows what the safety check says about a pattern, and `check`
143:   follows the same rules as the plugin (`--no-store` means the shared rules only: no store, no presets).
144: 
145: herdr is not in opencode's table of known programs, so an "always" answer to any herdr prompt is saved by opencode as
146: `herdr *`, for every agent until restart. The write guard still blocks the commands above, but nothing stops
147: `herdr pane send-text`. Answer "once" to herdr prompts. rtk does not rewrite herdr commands, so there are no `rtk herdr`
148: rules.
149: 
150: ## Options
151: 
152: Set them with the tuple form: `["opencode-readonly-guard", { … }]`.
153: 
154: | Option           | Default                                         | Meaning                                                         |
155: | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
156: | `agents.include` | `[]`                                            | extra agents to treat as read-only (they must exist)            |
157: | `agents.exclude` | `[]`                                            | agents to leave alone                                           |
158: | `allow`          | `[]`                                            | extra bash patterns to allow; each passes the same safety check |
159: | `presets`        | `{}`                                            | switch built-in rule sets on or off: `{ "herdr-ui": false }`    |
160: | `store`          | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/readonly-guard.json` | learned rules, dismissed candidates, agent lists                |
161: | `logDir`         | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/readonly-guard`        | `events.jsonl` (rotated at 5 MB to `events.old.jsonl`)          |
162: | `toast`          | `true`                                          | warn when an "always" answer is given in a read-only agent      |
163: | `command`        | `"guard-review"`                                | name of the review command, or `false` to not register it       |
164: 
165: `READONLY_GUARD_STORE` and `READONLY_GUARD_DATA` override the default paths (an explicit option wins). The store file
166: is plain JSON and safe to keep in your dotfiles; the event log contains the commands your agents ran, so keep it local.
167: The startup `init` event in the log lists the `presets` in effect next to the number of `learned` rules.
168: 
169: ## What it does not do
170: 
171: This is an accident preventer and a policy engine, not a sandbox.
172: 
173: - Only the `bash`/`shell` tool is covered. MCP tools, `webfetch` and others follow opencode's normal permissions.
174: - Interpreters can write (`python -c`, `node -e`, `awk`, `sqlite3 .shell`). They are not on the allowlist, so they
175:   prompt, but the guard does not read their code, and a broad "always" answer would let them through.
176: - Parsing is a hand-written approximation of POSIX shell; anything it cannot parse is blocked rather than guessed.
177: - Linux and macOS shells only. PowerShell is not parsed.
178: - "Always" answers made in opencode itself stay in effect for all agents until restart, see the findings below. The
179:   plugin warns, logs them and keeps the write guard on top, but it cannot revoke them.
180: 
181: ## Findings about opencode 1.19.3
182: 
183: What building this taught us. Each point was checked against the binary or by a live run, and several are worth an
184: upstream issue (they are in [TODO.md](TODO.md)).
185: 
186: **Permissions**
187: 
188: - Plan mode is a prompt. The `plan` agent only denies the `edit` tool (except plan files); its `bash` is `* allow`
189:   and so is `explore`'s. The "READ-ONLY phase" text is a reminder injected into the conversation.
190: - Rules are evaluated in order and the last match wins; `*` matches anything and a trailing ` *` also matches the bare
191:   command.
192: - Bash commands are split with tree-sitter and each simple command is matched on its own text. That text includes a
193:   redirection only when the command's direct parent is the redirection, so `cat a > b` is matched as written, while
194:   the redirections of later pipeline stages (`a | b > f`), `{ …; } > f` and `( … ) > f` are invisible to patterns.
195:   Glob rules therefore cannot stop those writes; a parser in `tool.execute.before` can.
196: - Commands inside `$(…)`, backticks and `<(…)` are checked as separate commands.
197: 
198: **"Always" answers**
199: 
200: - The saved pattern is the command prefix plus `*`, using a built-in table of how many words matter (`git log *`,
201:   `npm view *`) and falling back to the first word. Unknown programs become `prog *`: answering "always" to
202:   `tee /dev/null` allowed `tee *`, and for anything rewritten by the rtk plugin it is `rtk *`.
203: - It is kept in memory for the whole opencode process, is checked after every agent's rules (so it beats `ask` and
204:   `deny`), applies to all agents and sessions, and is lost on restart. The `permission` table in the database stays
205:   empty.
206: 
207: **Plugin API**
208: 
209: - `tool.execute.before` runs before the permission check; throwing from it aborts the tool call and the message reaches
210:   the model. This is what makes the write guard possible.
211: - The `permission.ask` hook is declared in the types and docs but is never called. A plugin cannot answer prompts
212:   itself, so learning has to go through a review step.
213: - The `config` hook may edit `agent.<name>.permission`; the rules end up after the built-in ones in the resolved
214:   agent (`opencode debug agent <name>` shows them). A permission set globally is appended after every agent's rules.
215: - `chat.params` reports the agent of each model call, including subagents. The utility agents `title`, `summary` and
216:   `compaction` share the session, so they must be ignored when tracking which agent a session belongs to. The v1 SDK
217:   types do not expose `agent` on sessions, but the runtime does (used as a fallback).
218: - Permission events are `permission.asked` / `permission.replied` at runtime, although the v1 SDK types still say
219:   `permission.updated`.
220: - Plugin tools can call `context.ask()` to raise a permission prompt. Agents start from `* allow`, so the plugin adds a
221:   global `readonly_guard_allow: ask` rule (evaluated after every agent's rules) to force the confirmation prompt.
222: 
223: **Plugin packaging (v1)**
224: 
225: - opencode treats every export of a plugin module as a plugin and calls it. Export only the default definition.
226: - A package is loaded from `exports["./server"]`, else `main`. A default export `{ id, server }` is supported since
227:   1.18.29. `engines.opencode` is enforced. Peer dependencies such as `@opencode-ai/plugin` are installed for you.
228: - opencode 2.x plugins are `Plugin.define({ id, setup })`, V1 plugins do not run there, and V2 has a real
229:   `permission.hook("evaluate")` that would remove most of these workarounds.
230: 
231: **Models and tooling**
232: 
233: - Models in plan mode often refuse to run a write command to "test" the guard, because of the reminder. To exercise
234:   it, delegate to `explore` from `build`, or use an `edit: deny` harness agent (see the e2e tests).
235: - The rtk plugin rewrites commands (`ls` → `rtk ls`) before permissions are evaluated, so patterns must match the
236:   rewritten form (the allowlist has `rtk …` entries). Models then see a command they did not write and retry it
237:   several times, which wastes tokens (observed with Haiku and Sonnet).
238: - When spawning `opencode run` from another program, set `PWD` to the working directory (opencode trusts it over the
239:   real cwd; a mismatch fails with an `UnknownError`).
240: 
241: ## Development
242: 
243: Everything is managed with [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev); Git hooks with [hk](https://hk.jdx.dev).
244: 
245: ```sh
246: mise install                # bun, node, hk, actionlint, shellcheck and the pinned opencode
247: mise run setup              # bun install + git hooks (prettier, oxlint, tsc, conventional commits)
248: mise run check              # lint, formatting, types, unit tests (what CI runs)
249: mise run test:integration   # builds, then drives the real opencode without a model, and a packed tarball
250: mise run test:e2e           # opt-in, real model: E2E_MODEL=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5
251: mise tasks                  # all tasks
252: ```
253: 
254: Code style follows opencode: TypeScript (strict, NodeNext), no semicolons, 120 columns, oxlint, prettier. See
255: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for adding rules and test cases.
256: 
257: ## License
258: 
259: [MIT](LICENSE), the same as opencode.

(End of file - total 259 lines)
</content>

<content>
1: # Contributing
2: 
3: Thanks for helping to make read-only agents trustworthy. The most useful contributions are **rules**: commands that
4: are safe to run without asking, flags that make a safe command unsafe, and test cases that pin the behaviour down.
5: 
6: ## Setup
7: 
8: ```sh
9: mise install        # bun, node, hk, actionlint, shellcheck, opencode (pinned in mise.toml)
10: mise run setup      # bun install + git hooks
11: mise run check      # what CI runs: lint, format, types, unit tests
12: ```
13: 
14: Without mise you need Bun 1.4+, Node 22+ and `bun install`; `bun run check` does the same as `mise run check`.
15: 
16: ## The shared rules
17: 
18: Everything the plugin decides on its own comes from the JSON files in [`rules/`](rules). They are editor-validated by
19: the JSON Schemas in [`rules/schema/`](rules/schema) and checked by the unit tests.
20: 
21: | File            | Contents                                                                                         |
22: | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
23: | `allow.json`    | opencode bash patterns that read-only agents may run without a prompt. Each has a `reason`.      |
24: | `ask.json`      | patterns that always ask, even when allowed above: flags that write files or run other programs. |
25: | `commands.json` | classification used by the write guard and the learning safety check (see below).                |
26: | `cases.json`    | expected verdicts for commands (`allow` / `ask` / `block`) and for patterns (`ok` true / false). |
27: 
28: Pattern syntax is opencode's: `*` matches anything, `?` one character, and a trailing ` *` also matches the bare
29: command. The **last matching rule wins**, which is why `ask.json` is applied after everything else.
30: 
31: ### Adding a command to the allowlist
32: 
33: An allow rule must be safe in **every** use the pattern can match, not just the common one.
34: 
35: 1. Look for options that write files, delete, or run other programs (`--output`, `-o FILE`, `-exec`, `--pre`, `-x`,
36:    `-i`, `--in-place`, `-delete`, …). If any exists, either do not allow the command, or add the dangerous option to
37:    `ask.json` (a prompt) and, if it is unambiguous, to the analyzer in `src/analyze.ts` (a block).
38: 2. Add the pattern and a short `reason` to `allow.json`. Use `cmd *` for "any arguments", `cmd sub*` for a family of
39:    subcommands, and the exact text for a single use.
40: 3. If the command is reached through the rtk plugin, add the `rtk …` form too.
41: 4. Add cases to `cases.json`: at least one `allow`, plus an `ask` or `block` case for each dangerous option.
42: 5. Run `mise run check`.
43: 
44: Other files:
45: 
46: - **`commands.json` → `hardWrite`:** commands that modify files whatever their arguments. They are blocked.
47: - **`commands.json` → `packageManagers`, `git`:** which subcommands write, and which git subcommands may get a
48:   wildcard rule from `/guard-review`.
49: - **`commands.json` → `herdr`:** `help` (printed help, allowed only as exact commands), `read` (read-only
50:   subcommands, a wildcard may follow), `ui` (what the `herdr-ui` preset in `src/sources.ts` allows inside herdr;
51:   never in `allow.json`) and `write` (blocked). Any other herdr subcommand must be added to `ask.json` as `herdr <sub> *`;
52:   there is no catch-all, because a `herdr *` ask rule would also silence the allowed reads. Keep the four lists
53:   disjoint and `allow.json` in step with `help` and `read` (the unit tests check both).
54: - **`commands.json` → `wildcardSafe`:** commands for which `/guard-review` may offer `cmd *`. Only add a command whose
55:   every read-only use is harmless and whose write options are covered by `ask.json` or the analyzer.
56: 
57: Behaviour that depends on arguments (`tee`, `sed -i`, `find -exec`, `curl -o`, `git branch <name>`, …) lives in
58: `src/analyze.ts`; add a unit test in `test/unit/analyze.test.ts` and a case in `cases.json`.
59: 
60: ## Tests
61: 
62: | Tier        | Command                     | Needs                                    |
63: | ----------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
64: | unit        | `mise run test`             | nothing                                  |
65: | integration | `mise run test:integration` | opencode on `PATH`; builds `dist/` first |
66: | e2e         | `mise run test:e2e`         | opencode credentials; costs a few cents  |
67: 
68: Unit tests include every case in `cases.json`, so a rule change is tested by adding a line there. Integration tests
69: load the built plugin (and a packed tarball) into the real opencode without calling a model. The e2e tests are
70: opt-in because they use a real model.
71: 
72: ## Commits and pull requests
73: 
74: - [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org), enforced by the `commit-msg` hook: `feat(rules): …`,
75:   `fix(analyze): …`, `docs: …`, `test: …`, `build: …`, `ci: …`, `chore: …`.
76: - One logical change per commit. A rule change and its `cases.json` entries go together.
77: - Update `CHANGELOG.md` for user-visible changes.
78: - The pre-commit hook (hk) runs prettier, oxlint, tsc, actionlint and whitespace checks; CI runs the same plus the
79:   tests. Please run `mise run check` before pushing.
80: 
81: ## Reporting a bypass
82: 
83: If a command writes from a read-only agent without being blocked or asked about, open an issue with the command, the
84: agent, and the opencode version. Add it to [`rules/cases.json`](rules/cases.json) as a failing case if you can.
85: 
86: By contributing you agree that your work is released under the [MIT license](LICENSE).

(End of file - total 86 lines)
</content>

8: ### Added

10: - Write guard for read-only agents (`plan`, `explore`, agents with `edit: deny`): blocks write redirections in any

17:   `readonly_guard_update` tools add vetted rules after an explicit confirmation of the exact pattern.
18: - `opencode-readonly-guard` command-line tool: `check`, `vet`, `rules`, `review`, `install`.
19: - Plugin options (`agents`, `allow`, `store`, `logDir`, `toast`, `command`).
20: - herdr rules: read-only `herdr` commands (`agent list`, `pane read`, `status`, …) are allowed in read-only agents;
21:   every other subcommand always asks and cannot be learned; `update`, `worktree create|remove`,
22:   `integration install|uninstall`, `session delete`, `plugin install|update`, `api schema --output` and `pane run` of a
23:   writing command are blocked.
24: - The `herdr-ui` preset: `herdr tab rename` and `herdr notification show`, which only change what herdr displays, are
25:   allowed when opencode runs in a herdr pane (`HERDR_ENV=1`) and not elsewhere. Switch it off with
26:   `"presets": { "herdr-ui": false }` in the plugin options, the store or herdr's own `readonly-guard.json` (in the
27:   directory of `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/herdr`; read only inside herdr, never written, the last
28:   source wins); `allow` patterns from these sources pass the same safety check. UI commands listed by the user only
29:   take effect inside herdr. The `init` log event gains the `presets` in effect.

145: function curlWrites(args: readonly string[]): string | null {

195:       const why = commandWrites(simple.words, depth)

10: /**

12:  *  - `block`: the write guard refuses it before any permission rule runs;
13:  *  - `ask`: some simple command in it needs the user's approval;
14:  *  - `allow`: every simple command is allowed without a prompt.
15:  *
16:  * opencode evaluates each simple command separately; this reproduces that on the parsed words, so quoting and
17:  * redirections are not part of the text the rules see (a close approximation of what opencode logs).

22:   for (const simple of simpleCommands(command)) {

24:   }

97:     if (event.type !== "replied" || event.reply !== "always" || event.permission !== "bash") continue
98:     for (const raw of event.patterns ?? []) {
99:       const pattern = normalizePattern(raw)
100:       if (store.dismissed.includes(pattern) || evaluate(pattern, bash) === "allow") continue
101:       const candidate = candidates.get(pattern) ?? {
102:         pattern,
103:         count: 0,
104:         agents: new Set<string>(),
105:         always: new Set<string>(),
106:         last: "",
107:       }
108:       candidate.count++
109:       if (event.agent) candidate.agents.add(event.agent)
110:       for (const always of event.always ?? []) candidate.always.add(always)
111:       candidate.last = event.ts
112:       candidates.set(pattern, candidate)
113:     }
114:   }
115:   const listed = [...candidates.values()]
116:     .toSorted((a, b) => b.count - a.count || b.last.localeCompare(a.last))
117:     .slice(0, limit)
118:   const shown = candidates.size > listed.length ? `, showing ${listed.length}` : ""
119:   out.push("", `### Candidates from "always" answers (${candidates.size}${shown})`)
120:   if (!listed.length) out.push("(none)")
121:   for (const [index, candidate] of listed.entries()) {
122:     const remembered = [...candidate.always].map((always) => `\`${always}\``).join(", ") || "-"
123:     out.push(
124:       `${index + 1}. \`${candidate.pattern}\`: ${candidate.count}×, agents: ${[...candidate.agents].join(", ")}, opencode remembered: ${remembered}`,
125:     )
126:     const choices = [{ kind: "exact", pattern: candidate.pattern }]
127:     const scoped = scopeToDirectory(candidate.pattern)
128:     if (scoped) choices.push({ kind: "directory", pattern: scoped })
129:     for (const always of candidate.always) choices.push({ kind: "general", pattern: normalizePattern(always) })
130:     const seen = new Set<string>()
131:     for (const option of choices) {
132:       if (seen.has(option.pattern)) continue
133:       seen.add(option.pattern)
134:       const verdict = vet(option.pattern)
135:       const caution = verdict.ok && verdict.note && verdict.note !== "exact command" ? ` (${verdict.note})` : ""
136:       const status = verdict.ok ? "[OK]" : `[REFUSED: ${verdict.reason}]`
137:       out.push(`   - ${status} ${option.kind}: \`${option.pattern}\`${caution}`)
138:     }
139:   }
140: 
141:   // Prompt statistics
142:   const stats = new Map<string, { once: number; always: number; reject: number }>()
143:   for (const event of events) {
144:     if (event.type !== "replied" || event.permission !== "bash") continue
145:     for (const pattern of event.patterns ?? []) {

148:       if (event.reply === "once" || event.reply === "always" || event.reply === "reject") entry[event.reply]++
149:       stats.set(head, entry)
150:     }
151:   }
152:   const top = [...stats.entries()].toSorted((a, b) => total(b[1]) - total(a[1])).slice(0, 15)
153:   out.push("", "### Prompts in read-only agents by command (once / always / reject)")
154:   if (!top.length) out.push("(none)")
155:   for (const [head, entry] of top) out.push(`- \`${head}\`: ${entry.once} / ${entry.always} / ${entry.reject}`)
156:   const suggestions = top.filter(

175:     blocks.set(reason, entry)

180:     out.push(`- ${entry.count}× ${reason}, e.g. \`${clip(entry.sample, 120)}\``)

Call ${TOOL_UPDATE} with action "allow" and the exact pattern; the user then confirms it in a permission prompt. Use action "dismiss" with the candidate pattern for rejected candidates.`,

4: /**
5:  * opencode's `Wildcard.match`: `*` matches anything, `?` one character, and a trailing ` *` also matches the bare
6:  * command (`ls *` matches `ls`). Backslashes are treated as path separators.
7:  */
8: export function wildcardMatch(input: string, pattern: string): boolean {
9:   const text = input.replaceAll("\\", "/")
10:   let source = pattern
11:     .replaceAll("\\", "/")
12:     .replace(/[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&")
13:     .replace(/\*/g, ".*")
14:     .replace(/\?/g, ".")
15:   if (source.endsWith(" .*")) source = source.slice(0, -3) + "( .*)?"
16:   return new RegExp(`^${source}$`, "s").test(text)
17: }
18: 
19: /** The action of the last matching rule (opencode evaluates permission rules in order, last match wins). */
20: export function evaluate(command: string, rules: readonly RuleEntry[], fallback: Action = "ask"): Action {
21:   let action = fallback
22:   for (const [pattern, ruleAction] of rules) if (wildcardMatch(command, pattern)) action = ruleAction
23:   return action
24: }

1: /**
2:  * A small POSIX-ish shell tokenizer. It does not execute or expand anything: it splits a command line into simple
3:  * commands (words + redirections) and collects the bodies of command substitutions so they can be analyzed too.
4:  *
5:  * Handled: quotes, escapes, comments, heredocs (bodies skipped), `$(…)`, backticks, process substitution,
6:  * `((…))`, `[[ … ]]`, pipes, lists, groups and subshells. Anything it cannot parse is reported as an error and
7:  * treated as unsafe by the analyzer.
8:  */

12:   op: string
13:   target: string
14: }
15:

17:   words: string[]
18:   redirs: Redirection[]
19: }
20: 
21: export interface ParsedShell {

23:   /** Bodies of `$(…)`, backtick and process substitutions found anywhere in the input. */
24:   subs: string[]
25:   error?: string
26: }

30: /** Index of the `close` that matches an already-opened `open`, skipping quotes and nesting; -1 if unbalanced. */
31: function closeIndex(src: string, start: number, open: string, close: string): number {
32:   let depth = 1
33:   let i = start
34:   while (i < src.length) {
35:     const c = src[i]
36:     if (c === "\\") {
37:       i += 2
38:       continue
39:     }
40:     if (c === "'") {
41:       const j = src.indexOf("'", i + 1)
42:       if (j < 0) return -1
43:       i = j + 1
44:       continue
45:     }
46:     if (c === '"') {
47:       let j = i + 1
48:       while (j < src.length && src[j] !== '"') j += src[j] === "\\" ? 2 : 1
49:       if (j >= src.length) return -1
50:       i = j + 1
51:       continue
52:     }
53:     if (c === "`") {
54:       const j = backtickIndex(src, i + 1)
55:       if (j < 0) return -1
56:       i = j + 1
57:       continue
58:     }
59:     if (c === open) depth++
60:     else if (c === close && --depth === 0) return i
61:     i++
62:   }
63:   return -1
64: }

71:       continue
72:     }

74:     i++
75:   }

86:   let heredocNext: boolean | null = null // next word is a heredoc delimiter (value: strip leading tabs)

129:       }

142:     }
143:     if (c === "$" && src[i + 1] === "'") {
144:       let j = i + 2
145:       while (j < n && src[j] !== "'") j += src[j] === "\\" ? 2 : 1
146:       if (j >= n) return fail("unbalanced $' quote")
147:       word += src.slice(i + 2, j)
148:       inWord = true
149:       i = j + 1
150:       continue
151:     }
152:     if (c === '"') {
153:       let j = i + 1
154:       let literal = ""
155:       while (j < n && src[j] !== '"') {
156:         if (src[j] === "\\") {
157:           literal += src[j + 1] ?? ""
158:           j += 2
159:           continue
160:         }
161:         if (src[j] === "$" && src[j + 1] === "(") {
162:           const k = closeIndex(src, j + 2, "(", ")")
163:           if (k < 0) return fail("unbalanced $(")
164:           addSub(src.slice(j + 2, k))
165:           literal += "$(…)"
166:           j = k + 1
167:           continue
168:         }
169:         if (src[j] === "`") {
170:           const k = backtickIndex(src, j + 1)
171:           if (k < 0) return fail("unbalanced backtick")
172:           subs.push(src.slice(j + 1, k))
173:           literal += "`…`"
174:           j = k + 1
175:           continue
176:         }
177:         literal += src[j]
178:         j++
179:       }
180:       if (j >= n) return fail("unbalanced double quote")
181:       word += literal
182:       inWord = true
183:       i = j + 1
184:       continue
185:     }
186:     if (c === "$" && src[i + 1] === "(") {
187:       const k = closeIndex(src, i + 2, "(", ")")
188:       if (k < 0) return fail("unbalanced $(")
189:       addSub(src.slice(i + 2, k))
190:       word += "$(…)"
191:       inWord = true
192:       i = k + 1
193:       continue
194:     }
195:     if (c === "$" && src[i + 1] === "{") {
196:       const k = closeIndex(src, i + 2, "{", "}")
197:       if (k < 0) return fail("unbalanced ${")
198:       word += src.slice(i, k + 1)
199:       inWord = true
200:       i = k + 1
201:       continue
202:     }
203:     if (c === "`") {
204:       const k = backtickIndex(src, i + 1)
205:       if (k < 0) return fail("unbalanced backtick")
206:       subs.push(src.slice(i + 1, k))
207:       word += "`…`"
208:       inWord = true
209:       i = k + 1
210:       continue
211:     }
212:     if (c === "#" && !inWord) {
213:       while (i < n && src[i] !== "\n") i++
214:       continue
215:     }
216:     if (c === " " || c === "\t" || c === "\r") {
217:       pushWord()
218:       i++
219:       continue
220:     }
221:     if (c === "\n") {
222:       endCommand()
223:       i++
224:       for (const h of heredocs.splice(0)) {
225:         while (i < n) {
226:           const nl = src.indexOf("\n", i)
227:           const end = nl < 0 ? n : nl
228:           const line = src.slice(i, end)
229:           i = end + 1
230:           if ((h.strip ? line.replace(/^\t+/, "") : line) === h.delim) break
231:         }
232:       }
233:       continue
234:     }
235:     if ((c === "<" || c === ">") && src[i + 1] === "(") {
236:       const k = closeIndex(src, i + 2, "(", ")")
237:       if (k < 0) return fail("unbalanced process substitution")
238:       addSub(src.slice(i + 2, k))
239:       if (c === ">") cur.redirs.push({ op: ">(", target: "(process substitution)" })
240:       word += `${c}(…)`
241:       inWord = true
242:       i = k + 1
243:       continue
244:     }
245:     if (inDoubleBracket && (c === "<" || c === ">")) {
246:       word += c
247:       inWord = true
248:       i++
249:       continue
250:     }
251:     if (c === ">" || c === "<" || (c === "&" && src[i + 1] === ">")) {
252:       let fd = ""
253:       if (inWord && /^(\d+|\{[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\})$/.test(word)) {
254:         fd = word
255:         word = ""
256:         inWord = false
257:       } else {
258:         pushWord()
259:       }
260:       const op = REDIRECT_OPERATORS.find((candidate) => src.startsWith(candidate, i))!
261:       i += op.length
262:       if (op === "<<" || op === "<<-") {
263:         heredocNext = op === "<<-"
264:         continue
265:       }
266:       pending = fd + op
267:       continue
268:     }
269:     if (c === "|") {
270:       endCommand()
271:       i += src[i + 1] === "|" || src[i + 1] === "&" ? 2 : 1
272:       continue
273:     }
274:     if (c === "&") {
275:       endCommand()
276:       i += src[i + 1] === "&" ? 2 : 1
277:       continue
278:     }
279:     if (c === ";") {
280:       endCommand()
281:       i += src[i + 1] === ";" ? 2 : 1
282:       continue
283:     }
284:     if (c === "(") {
285:       if (inWord) {
286:         word += c // name() or arr=(
287:         i++
288:         continue
289:       }
290:       if (src[i + 1] === "(") {
291:         const k = closeIndex(src, i + 1, "(", ")") // (( arithmetic ))
292:         if (k < 0) return fail("unbalanced ((")
293:         endCommand()
294:         i = k + 1
295:         continue
296:       }
297:       endCommand()
298:       i++
299:       continue
300:     }
301:     if (c === ")") {
302:       endCommand()
303:       i++
304:       continue
305:     }
306:     word += c
307:     inWord = true
308:     i++
309:   }
310:   endCommand()
311:   return { cmds, subs }
312: }
313: 
314: /**
315:  * Every simple command in the input as the text opencode's permission rules would see it (approximately:
316:  * words joined by single spaces, redirections omitted), including those inside command substitutions.
317:  */
318: export function simpleCommands(src: string, depth = 0): string[] {
319:   if (depth > 5) return []
320:   const parsed = parseShell(src)
321:   const out = parsed.cmds.filter((cmd) => cmd.words.length).map((cmd) => cmd.words.join(" "))
322:   for (const sub of parsed.subs) out.push(...simpleCommands(sub, depth + 1))
323:   return out
324: }

1: import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs"
2: import { classifyPattern, isHerdrUiPattern, normalizePattern } from "./classify.js"
3: import type { Commands } from "./rules.js"
4: import { switches, type StoreData } from "./store.js"
5: 
6: /** A rule set the plugin ships but the user can switch on or off, kept apart from the shared allowlist. */
7: export interface Preset {
8:   /** The name used in the `presets` option and in the store. */
9:   id: string
10:   summary: string
11:   enabledByDefault: boolean
12:   /** Only has an effect when opencode runs in a herdr pane (`HERDR_ENV=1`). */
13:   insideHerdrOnly: boolean
14:   patterns(commands: Commands): string[]
15: }
16: 
17: export const PRESETS: readonly Preset[] = [
18:   {
19:     id: "herdr-ui",
20:     summary: "herdr commands that only change what herdr displays (a tab label, a notification)",
21:     enabledByDefault: true,
22:     insideHerdrOnly: true,
23:     patterns: ({ herdr }) => herdr.ui.map((path) => `herdr ${path} *`),
24:   },
25: ]
26: 
27: export interface SourceProblem {
28:   /** Which source the problem comes from: `store`, `options` or `presets`. */
29:   where: string
30:   pattern?: string
31:   error: string
32: }
33: 
34: export interface Effective {
35:   /** Everything allowed on top of the shared allowlist: the presets' patterns, then the user's. */
36:   patterns: string[]
37:   /** The user's own patterns that apply (store and options), without the presets'. */
38:   learned: string[]
39:   /** The presets in effect. */
40:   presets: string[]
41:   /** Values that were ignored, to be logged. */
42:   problems: SourceProblem[]
43: }
44: 
45: /** The rules file in herdr's config directory: preset switches and extra patterns, for herdr only. */
46: export interface HerdrRules {
47:   allow: string[]
48:   presets: Record<string, boolean>
49: }
50: 
51: const HERDR_WHERE = "herdr config"
52: 
53: /**
54:  * Read the rules file in herdr's config directory. It is only looked at inside herdr, a missing file is no file,
55:  * and the plugin never writes it (`/guard-review` only writes the store). A corrupt file is reported and ignored.
56:  */
57: export function loadHerdrRules(
58:   { insideHerdr, herdrFile }: { insideHerdr: boolean; herdrFile: string },
59:   onError?: (error: Error) => void,
60: ): HerdrRules {
61:   const none: HerdrRules = { allow: [], presets: {} }
62:   if (!insideHerdr || !existsSync(herdrFile)) return none
63:   try {
64:     const raw = JSON.parse(readFileSync(herdrFile, "utf8")) as Record<string, unknown>
65:     return {
66:       allow: Array.isArray(raw.allow) ? raw.allow.filter((item): item is string => typeof item === "string") : [],
67:       presets: switches(raw.presets),
68:     }
69:   } catch (error) {
70:     onError?.(new Error(`cannot parse ${herdrFile}`, { cause: error }))
71:     return none
72:   }
73: }
74: 
75: export interface EffectiveInput {
76:   commands: Commands
77:   store: Pick<StoreData, "allow" | "presets">
78:   options: { allow: readonly string[]; presets: Readonly<Record<string, boolean>>; insideHerdr: boolean }
79:   /** The rules file from herdr's config directory, if any (see `loadHerdrRules`). */
80:   herdr?: HerdrRules
81: }
82: 
83: /**
84:  * Combine the sources of allow rules into what a read-only agent gets on top of the shared allowlist.
85:  *
86:  * - Every user pattern passes the same safety check as a learned rule.
87:  * - herdr UI patterns only take effect inside herdr: outside a pane the herdr CLI still reaches the running session
88:  *   and acts on whatever is focused there.
89:  * - herdr's own file may only hold `herdr …` patterns, and is ignored outside herdr.
90:  * - A preset is on when its default says so and no source switches it off. When sources disagree, the later one
91:  *   wins: plugin options, then the store, then herdr's file.
92:  */
93: export function effectiveRules({ commands, store, options, herdr }: EffectiveInput): Effective {
94:   const problems: SourceProblem[] = []
95:   const vet = (patterns: readonly string[], where: string): string[] =>
96:     patterns.map(normalizePattern).filter((pattern) => {
97:       const verdict = classifyPattern(pattern, commands)
98:       if (!verdict.ok) problems.push({ where, pattern, error: `ignored rule: ${verdict.reason}` })
99:       return verdict.ok
100:     })
101:   const applies = (pattern: string): boolean => options.insideHerdr || !isHerdrUiPattern(pattern, commands)
102:   const fromHerdr = options.insideHerdr && herdr ? herdr : { allow: [], presets: {} }
103:   const herdrOnly = fromHerdr.allow.map(normalizePattern).filter((pattern) => {
104:     if (pattern.startsWith("herdr ")) return true
105:     problems.push({ where: HERDR_WHERE, pattern, error: "ignored rule: only herdr commands belong in this file" })
106:     return false
107:   })
108:   const learned = [
109:     ...vet(store.allow, "store"),
110:     ...vet(options.allow, "options"),
111:     ...vet(herdrOnly, HERDR_WHERE),
112:   ].filter(applies)
113: 
114:   const switched = new Map<string, boolean>()
115:   for (const [where, table] of [
116:     ["presets", options.presets],
117:     ["presets", store.presets],
118:     [HERDR_WHERE, fromHerdr.presets],
119:   ] as const) {
120:     for (const [id, on] of Object.entries(table)) {
121:       if (PRESETS.some((preset) => preset.id === id)) switched.set(id, on)
122:       else problems.push({ where, error: `unknown preset "${id}" ignored` })
123:     }
124:   }
125:   const active = PRESETS.filter(
126:     (preset) =>
127:       (switched.get(preset.id) ?? preset.enabledByDefault) && (options.insideHerdr || !preset.insideHerdrOnly),
128:   )
129:   return {
130:     patterns: [...active.flatMap((preset) => preset.patterns(commands)), ...learned],
131:     learned,
132:     presets: active.map((preset) => preset.id),
133:     problems,
134:   }
135: }

62:       const agent = (response.data as { agent?: unknown } | undefined)?.agent

124:         project: worktree,
125:         command: clip(command),
126:       }
127:       if (verdict.block) {

2: import { join } from "node:path"
3: 
4: export interface LogEvent {
5:   ts: string
6:   type: string
7:   agent?: string
8:   project?: string
9:   sessionID?: string
10:   callID?: string
11:   requestID?: string
12:   command?: string
13:   reason?: string
14:   permission?: string
15:   patterns?: string[]
16:   always?: string[]
17:   reply?: string
18:   [key: string]: unknown
19: }
20: 
21: export interface GuardLog {
22:   readonly file: string
23:   /** Append one event. Never throws: logging must not break a tool call. */
24:   write(event: Omit<LogEvent, "ts">): void
25:   /** All events, oldest first (the rotated file, then the current one). */
26:   read(): LogEvent[]
27: }
28: 
29: export const clip = (text: string, max = 2000): string => (text.length > max ? `${text.slice(0, max)}…` : text)
30: 
31: /** A JSON-lines event log in `dir/events.jsonl`, rotated to `events.old.jsonl` past `maxBytes`. */
32: export function createLog(dir: string, maxBytes = 5 * 1024 * 1024): GuardLog {
33:   const file = join(dir, "events.jsonl")
34:   const rotated = join(dir, "events.old.jsonl")
35:   let writes = 0
36:   return {
37:     file,
38:     write(event) {
39:       try {
40:         mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
41:         if (writes++ % 100 === 0 && existsSync(file) && statSync(file).size > maxBytes) renameSync(file, rotated)
42:         appendFileSync(file, `${JSON.stringify({ ts: new Date().toISOString(), ...event })}\n`)
43:       } catch {
44:         // ignored on purpose
45:       }
46:     },
47:     read() {
48:       const events: LogEvent[] = []
49:       for (const path of [rotated, file]) {
50:         if (!existsSync(path)) continue
51:         for (const line of readFileSync(path, "utf8").split("\n")) {
52:           if (!line) continue
53:           try {
54:             events.push(JSON.parse(line) as LogEvent)
55:           } catch {
56:             // skip a corrupt line
57:           }
58:         }
59:       }
60:       return events
61:     },
62:   }
63: }

119:     return EXIT.usage
120:   }
121:   const options = resolveOptions({ store: takeValue(args, "--store"), logDir: takeValue(args, "--log-dir") }, io.env)
122:   io.out(
123:     `${review({
124:       store: loadStore(options.storeFile),
125:       events: createLog(options.logDir).read(),
126:       rules: loadRules(),
127:       limit,
128:       options,
129:       herdr: loadHerdrRules(options),
130:     })}\n`,
131:   )
132:   return 0
133: }
134: 
135: function install(args: string[], io: CliIo): number {
136:   const flags: string[] = []
137:   if (takeFlag(args, "-g", "--global")) flags.push("--global")
138:   if (takeFlag(args, "-f", "--force")) flags.push("--force")
139:   return io.run("opencode", ["plugin", PLUGIN_ID, ...flags])
140: }
141: 
142: /** Entry point of the command-line tool; returns the exit status. */
143: export function runCli(argv: readonly string[], io: CliIo): number {
144:   const args = [...argv]
145:   const command = args.shift()
146:   try {
147:     if (!command || command === "-h" || command === "--help" || command === "help") {
148:       io.out(HELP)
149:       return command ? 0 : EXIT.usage
150:     }
151:     if (command === "-v" || command === "--version") {
152:       io.out(`${version()}\n`)
153:       return 0
154:     }
155:     switch (command) {
156:       case "check":
157:         return check(args, io)
158:       case "vet":
159:         return vet(args, io)
160:       case "rules":
161:         return printRules(args, io)
162:       case "review":
163:         return printReview(args, io)
164:       case "install":
165:         return install(args, io)
166:       default:
167:         io.err(`unknown command: ${command}\n\n${HELP}`)
168:         return EXIT.usage
169:     }
170:   } catch (error) {
171:     io.err(`error: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}\n`)
172:     return 70
173:   }
174: }
175: 
176: /** The real environment: stdout, stderr and child processes. */
177: export function systemIo(): CliIo {
178:   return {
179:     out: (text) => void process.stdout.write(text),
180:     err: (text) => void process.stderr.write(text),
181:     env: process.env,
182:     run: (command, args) => spawnSync(command, args, { stdio: "inherit" }).status ?? 1,
183:   }
184: }

\"[redacted:worktrees_root]/rog-rules\"\nconst detail = process.argv.includes(\"--detail\") ? process.argv[process.argv.indexOf(\"--detail\") + 1] : undefined\nconst showAll = process.argv.includes(\"--all\")\nconst { decide } = await import(`${worktree}/dist/decide.js`)\nconst { buildBashRules, loadRules } = await import(`${worktree}/dist/rules.js`)\nconst bash = buildBashRules(loadRules(), [])\n\nconst LOG = \"~/.local/share/opencode/readonly-guard/events.jsonl\"\nconst events = readFileSync(LOG, \"utf8\")\n  .split(\"\\n\")\n  .filter(Boolean)\n  .map((line) => {\n    try {\n      return JSON.parse(line)\n    } catch {\n      return null\n    }\n  })\n  .filter(Boolean)\n\nconst MULTI = new Set([\n  \"git\", \"npm\", \"pnpm\", \"bun\", \"mise\", \"herdr\", \"docker\", \"podman\", \"systemctl\", \"rtk\", \"gh\", \"cargo\", \"ip\",\n  \"pacman\", \"flatpak\", \"snap\", \"virsh\", \"VBoxManage\", \"vagrant\", \"journalctl\", \"uv\", \"pip\", \"opencode\", \"hk\",\n])\n\nfunction head(text: string): string {\n  const words = text.trim().split(/\\s+/)\n  let i = 0\n  const prefix: string[] = []\n  while (i < words.length && /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/.test(words[i])) {\n    prefix.push(\"VAR=\")\n    i++\n  }\n  const w = words.slice(i)\n  if (prefix.length) return `<env-prefix> ${w[0] ?? \"\"}`\n  if (w[0] === \"rtk\") return `rtk ${head(w.slice(1).join(\" \"))}`\n  if (w[0] === \"git\" && w[1] && w[1].startsWith(\"-\")) return `git ${w[1]}`\n  if (MULTI.has(w[0]) && w[1] && !w[1].startsWith(\"-\")) return `${w[0]} ${w[1]}`\n  if (MULTI.has(w[0]) && w[1]) return `${w[0]} ${w[1]}`\n  return w[0] ?? \"\"\n}\n\nconst counts = new Map<string, { occ: number; uniq: Set<string>; agents: Set<string> }>()\nconst blocks = new Map<string, number>()\nlet asked = 0\nlet askedAsk = 0\nconst unique = new Set<string>()\nfor (const event of events) {\n  if (event.type !== \"asked\" || event.permission !== \"bash\") continue\n  asked++\n  let anyAsk = false\n  for (const pattern of event.patterns ?? []) {\n    unique.add(pattern)\n    const decision = decide(pattern, bash)\n    if (decision.verdict === \"block\") {\n      blocks.set(`${decision.reason} :: ${pattern.slice(0, 100)}`, (blocks.get(`${decision.reason} :: ${pattern.slice(0, 100)}`) ?? 0) + 1)\n      continue\n    }\n    if (decision.verdict !== \"ask\") continue\n    anyAsk = true\n    const prompt: string = decision.prompts ?? pattern\n    const key = head(prompt)\n    const entry = counts.get(key) ?? { occ: 0, uniq: new Set(), agents: new Set() }\n    entry.occ++\n    entry.uniq.add(prompt)\n    if (event.agent) entry.agents.add(event.agent)\n    counts.set(key, entry)\n  }\n  if (anyAsk) askedAsk++\n}\n\nconst sorted = [...counts.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1].occ - a[1].occ)\nconsole.log(`asked bash events: ${asked}, with >=1 ask stage: ${askedAsk}, unique patterns: ${unique.size}`)\nconsole.log(`groups: ${sorted.length}, total ask occurrences: ${sorted.reduce((n, [, e]) => n + e.occ, 0)}`)\nfor (const [key, entry] of sorted) {\n  if (detail && key !== detail) continue\n  console.log(`${String(entry.occ).padStart(4)} ${String(entry.uniq.size).padStart(3)}u  ${key}`)\n  if (detail || showAll) for (const u of entry.uniq) console.log(`         · ${u.replaceAll(\"\\n\", \"⏎\").slice(0, 160)}`)\n}\nif (blocks.size) {\n  console.log(\"\\nblocked stages:\")\n  for (const [k, n] of blocks) console.log(`${String(n).padStart(4)}  ${k.replaceAll(\"\\n\", \"⏎\")}`)\n}\n"
}

## Assistant (Build · Claude Opus 5.5 · 315.5s)

_Thinking:_
I notice `--delete-excluded` triggers an ask because of a broad `*-delete*` pattern false-matching, and similarly `df -h --output=avail` gets flagged since `* --output*` matches regardless — meaning adding `df *` wouldn't actually fix that case since the broader ask pattern overrides it.

Since `--output` is just a formatting flag, not a real risk, but reordering ask.json isn't feasible since it comes last in precedence, I'll just flag this as an open edge case rather than try to fix it, since narrowing the generic `--output` pattern could break coverage for other tools like curl or sort.

I'm also noticing `tee /dev/stderr` gets asked about since only `tee /dev/null` is exact-allowed — I could add `/dev/stderr` and `/dev/stdout` as additional safe exact matches, though this feels like a minor, optional addition rather than a core fix.

  -V, --version

----
Rewrite a raw command to its RTK equivalent (single source of truth for hooks)

Exit codes (a hook must handle all four). The rules are Claude Code's permission rules, checked against every command in a chain.

0 - rewrite printed, allow rules cover every command: the hook may auto-allow it. RTK_REWRITE_HOST=openclaw, for a delegate that gates commands itself, turns every 3 but an ask rule's into 0, so a hook that auto-allows on 0 runs rtk with that variable unset.

1 - nothing printed, no rewrite (no RTK equivalent, nothing left to rewrite, a command excluded in config, a construct RTK does not rewrite such as `$(...)` or a file redirect, or a deny rule matched inside a shell wrapper's script): run the command unchanged.

2 - a deny matched (checked before anything else). Nothing printed: a deny rule, defer to the agent's own deny. A message printed: an rtk pipeline rule denied or routed the command, block it with that message.

3 - rewrite printed, an ask rule matched or allow rules do not cover every command, including when there are no rules at all: use the rewrite and defer approval to the host.

Compare the rewrite with the original: a command already in RTK form can come back as itself under 0 or 3.

Exit 3 is still a rewrite, so `REWRITTEN=$(rtk rewrite "$CMD") || exit 0` drops it.

See hooks/claude/rtk-rewrite.sh in the RTK repository for reference handling.

Usage: rtk rewrite [OPTIONS] [ARGS]...


```

4: export interface StoreData {
5:   /** Learned bash patterns allowed in read-only agents. */
6:   allow: string[]
7:   /** Candidates the user does not want to see again. */
8:   dismissed: string[]

17:   "'presets' = built-in rule sets switched on or off, e.g. { \"herdr-ui\": false }. Applied at opencode startup."
18: 
19: const strings = (value: unknown): string[] =>
20:   Array.isArray(value) ? value.filter((item): item is string => typeof item === "string") : []
21: 
22: /** The entries of `value` that are booleans (a preset switch table). */
23: export const switches = (value: unknown): Record<string, boolean> =>
24:   typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
25:     ? Object.fromEntries(

27:       )
28:     : {}
29: 
30: export const emptyStore = (): StoreData => ({
31:   allow: [],
32:   dismissed: [],
33:   agents: { include: [], exclude: [] },
34:   presets: {},
35: })
36: 
37: /**
38:  * Read the learned-rules file. A missing file is an empty store. A corrupt file throws, unless `onError` is given,

40:  */
41: export function loadStore(file: string, onError?: (error: Error) => void): StoreData {
42:   if (!existsSync(file)) return emptyStore()
43:   try {
44:     const raw = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, "utf8")) as Record<string, unknown>
45:     const agents = (raw.agents ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>
46:     return {
47:       allow: strings(raw.allow),
48:       dismissed: strings(raw.dismissed),
49:       agents: { include: strings(agents.include), exclude: strings(agents.exclude) },
50:       presets: switches(raw.presets),
51:     }
52:   } catch (error) {

63:   const { presets, ...rest } = data
64:   // keep files that never used presets as they were
65:   const body = Object.keys(presets).length ? { ...rest, presets } : rest
66:   writeFileSync(`${file}.tmp`, `${JSON.stringify({ $comment: COMMENT, ...body }, null, 2)}\n`)

4: 
5: /** The parts of opencode's config this plugin edits. */
6: export interface MutableConfig {
7:   agent?: Record<string, AgentConfig | undefined>
8:   permission?: unknown
9:   command?: Record<string, unknown>
10:   [key: string]: unknown
11: }
12: 
13: export interface AgentConfig {

15:   permission?: unknown
16:   tools?: Record<string, boolean>
17:   [key: string]: unknown
18: }
19: 
20: export interface InjectInput {
21:   rules: RuleSet
22:   /** Learned and option-supplied patterns, already vetted. */
23:   learned: readonly string[]
24:   include: readonly string[]
25:   exclude: readonly string[]
26: }
27: 
28: type PermissionTable = Record<string, unknown>
29: 
30: const ACTIONS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["allow", "ask", "deny"])
31: 
32: /** opencode accepts `"allow"` or `{ pattern: action }` for a permission; normalize to the object form. */
33: function asTable(value: unknown): PermissionTable {
34:   if (value === undefined || value === null) return {}
35:   if (typeof value === "string") return { "*": value }
36:   return { ...(value as PermissionTable) }
37: }
38: 
39: function ownBashRules(value: unknown): RuleEntry[] {
40:   return Object.entries(asTable(value)).filter((entry): entry is [string, Action] => ACTIONS.has(String(entry[1])))
41: }
42: 
43: /** Is edit denied for this agent (so that it is meant to be read-only)? */
44: export function isEditDenied(agent: AgentConfig | undefined): boolean {
45:   if (!agent) return false
46:   const permission = agent.permission
47:   if (permission === "deny") return true
48:   if (agent.tools?.edit === false) return true
49:   if (typeof permission !== "object" || permission === null) return false
50:   const edit = (permission as PermissionTable).edit
51:   return edit === "deny" || (typeof edit === "object" && edit !== null && (edit as PermissionTable)["*"] === "deny")
52: }
53: 
54: /**
55:  * Add the read-only bash policy to every read-only agent and return their names.
56:  *
57:  * Read-only agents are `plan`, `explore`, agents with `edit: deny`, and `include`, minus `exclude`. Unknown agents
58:  * named in `include` are not created. An agent whose bash is fully denied stays that way.
59:  */
60: export function injectRules(config: MutableConfig, input: InjectInput): Set<string> {
61:   config.agent ??= {}
62:   const names = new Set<string>([...DEFAULT_READ_ONLY_AGENTS, ...input.include])
63:   for (const [name, agent] of Object.entries(config.agent)) if (isEditDenied(agent)) names.add(name)
64:   for (const name of input.exclude) names.delete(name)
65: 
66:   const readOnly = new Set<string>()
67:   for (const name of names) {
68:     const known = config.agent[name]
69:     if (!known && !DEFAULT_READ_ONLY_AGENTS.includes(name)) continue
70:     const agent = (config.agent[name] ??= {})
71:     if (agent.disable) continue
72:     const permission = asTable(agent.permission)
73:     const own = ownBashRules(permission.bash)
74:     if (!own.some(([pattern, action]) => pattern === "*" && action === "deny")) {
75:       permission.bash = Object.fromEntries(
76:         buildBashRules(
77:           input.rules,
78:           input.learned,
79:           own.filter(([pattern]) => pattern !== "*"),
80:         ),
81:       )
82:     }
83:     permission[TOOL_REVIEW] = "deny"
84:     permission[TOOL_UPDATE] = "deny"
85:     agent.permission = permission
86:     readOnly.add(name)
87:   }
88: 
89:   const plan = config.agent.plan
90:   if (readOnly.has("plan") && plan) {
91:     const permission = asTable(plan.permission)
92:     const task = asTable(permission.task)
93:     delete task["*"]
94:     permission.task = {
95:       "*": "ask",
96:       ...task,
97:       general: "deny",
98:       ...Object.fromEntries([...readOnly].filter((name) => name !== "plan").map((name) => [name, "allow"])),
99:     }
100:     plan.permission = permission
101:   }
102: 
103:   // Appended after every agent's own rules, so it prompts even under `"*": "allow"`.
104:   config.permission = { ...asTable(config.permission), [PERMISSION_CONFIRM]: "ask" }
105:   return readOnly
106: }

*/\nfunction dateSets(args: readonly string[]): boolean {\n  for (let j = 0; j < args.length; j++) {\n    const arg = args[j]\n    if (arg === \"--\") return args.slice(j + 1).some((operand) => !operand.startsWith(\"+\"))\n    if (arg === \"-\" || !arg.startsWith(\"-\")) {\n      if (!arg.startsWith(\"+\")) return true\n    } else if (arg.startsWith(\"--\")) {\n      const [name, value] = arg.slice(2).split(/=(.*)/s)\n      const matches = DATE_LONG.filter((option) => option.startsWith(name))\n      const option = DATE_LONG.includes(name) ? ## Assistant (Build · Claude Opus 5.5 · 39.6s)

_Thinking:_
I should add "set" to the write subcommands list for package managers, which would block commands like `mise set K=V`, `npm set k v`, and `yarn set version x` since that last one writes to .yarnrc. Checking other tools like bun, pip, uv, and cargo, none of them have a conflicting plain "set" subcommand to worry about.

For npm view, I need to worry about nopt's abbreviation support — since npm config options allow partial matches, something like `--cach` could resolve to `--cache` and `--logs-d` could resolve to `--logs-dir`, so I need glob patterns that catch these abbreviated forms too, while being careful not to over-match unrelated keys like `--ca` which is a legitimate certificate authority config option.

I'm also checking that env var prefixes like `npm_config_cache=` are already covered by the broader env prefix rule, and ruling out other npm view concerns like aliases (info/show/v), `--prefix`, `--userconfig`, and shrinkwrap interactions since none of those apply to a read-only view command.

Now I'm listing exact mise command forms: `mise --version`, `mise ls *`, `mise ls-remote *`, `mise tasks` with its subcommands (ls/info/deps), `mise settings` with ls/get, and `mise config` with ls/get. I'm also noting mise's global flags like `-C DIR`, `-E ENV`, `--raw`, `--locked`, `-y`, and `-j` that could trail these commands, and flagging the edge case of `mise ls --` followed by extra arguments as something to watch for.

Actually a bigger risk just occurred to me: the `-y` flag auto-answers "yes" to confirmation prompts, which could include mise's trust prompt for untrusted config files. If `mise ls -y` in a repo with an untrusted config auto-trusts it, that's a real state-changing side effect — it would persist trust info and enable template execution from that config, so I need to treat that combination as unsafe rather than a pure read.

I'm thinking through how mise behaves non-interactively when a config isn't trusted — it errors out unless `-y` is passed, which auto-trusts it. I want the analyzer to flag `--yes` or short flag clusters containing `y` as a candidate write action, since it silently accepts trust/install prompts, though catching bundled short flags reliably is tricky.

I realize bundled flags like `-qy` slip past the glob since it only catches the trailing `*` pattern, but that gap isn't easily fixable with simple glob matching. The real risk is an agent running mise in an untrusted repo, which would auto-trust the config and evaluate templates that could execute arbitrary commands.

I should also check whether `MISE_YES`/`--yes` actually controls trust behavior — from what I recall of mise's source, the trust prompt is skipped and auto-trusted when the `yes` setting is enabled, confirming that `-y` flags are indeed the dangerous ones to flag.

I'm now going through the various mise and npm subcommands to classify as read-only allow entries: things like `mise settings get`, `mise ls --prunable`, `mise tasks ls --all`, `mise tasks info`, `mise tasks deps`, `mise config get -f`, `mise config ls --tracked-configs`, plus npm version lookups, all look safe to permit in the cases file.

I'm also sorting the write/ambiguous commands into the ask category — things like `npm view` with custom cache/log paths, `mise run`/`mise tasks run`/`mise tasks add`, and settings-mutating commands like `mise settings experimental true` or `mise settings set`, which shouldn't be auto-allowed since they can modify config or execute tasks.

Then I'm flagging clear-cut blocks: commands like `mise set FOO=1` or `npm set fund false` that explicitly mutate state should be blocked outright.

## Map

`src/`

- `index.ts`: the module's only export, `{ id, server }`.
- `plugin.ts`: the opencode hooks: `config` (inject the rules, register `/guard-review`), `tool.execute.before` (the
  write guard), `event` (log prompts and answers), `chat.params` (which agent owns a session).
- `shell.ts`: POSIX-ish tokenizer (simple commands, redirections, substitutions); what it cannot parse is blocked.
- `analyze.ts`: the write guard: redirections, wrappers, `sed -i`, `find -delete`, git and package-manager writes, …
- `wildcard.ts`: opencode's pattern matching, last match wins. `decide.ts`: allow, ask or block for a command line.
- `rules.ts`: loads `rules/*.json` and builds the ordered bash rule list. `inject.ts`: finds the read-only agents and
  writes their rules into opencode's config.
- `classify.ts`: the safety check for patterns (learned rules, the `allow` option, `vet`).
- `sources.ts`: presets (`herdr-ui`) and the merge of options, store and herdr's file. `options.ts`: plugin options
  and default paths.

- `review.ts`, `tools.ts`, `command.ts`: the log summary, the `readonly_guard_review` and `readonly_guard_update`
  tools, the `/guard-review` command.
- `commands.ts`, `cli.ts`: the command-line tool. `constants.ts`: ids and tool names.

`rules/`: `allow.json`, `ask.json`, `commands.json`, `cases.json` and their JSON Schemas in `schema/` (CONTRIBUTING.md

Now only listing, `show` and `get-url` pass.\n- A sole trailing `--help` after a git, herdr, npm or mise subcommand path is not that subcommand's write (`herdr worktree create --help`, `npm install --help`). `-h` and `--help` next to other arguments are judged as before.\n- git branch and tag, checked against git 2.53:\n  - `-v`, `-vv`, `--verbose`, `--sort`, `--format` and `--color` do not switch to list mode, so `git branch -v NAME` and `git tag --sort=x NAME` create a ref. The guard used to let them through; it now blocks them.\n  - Write options are also caught when abbreviated (`git branch -a --edit-desc` edits the description) and in bundles (`-rd`).\n  - `git tag -n1 NAME`, which only lists, is no longer blocked.\n- `git ls-remote --upload-pack/--exec=CMD` is blocked when CMD writes.\n- `sort`:\n  - `--o`/`--out` abbreviations of `--output` are blocked like `-o`.\n  - `--compress-program=PROG` is blocked when PROG writes (compressors pass).\n- `uniq`: the OUTPUT operand is now parsed correctly. `uniq - out`, `uniq in 5` and `uniq -- -x out` were missed; `-` or the null device as OUTPUT is fine.\n- `date -s/--set` (any abbreviation) and a `MMDDhhmm` operand are blocked. Option values are parsed, so `date -d tomorrow` passes.\n- `hostname NAME`, `-F/--file` and `-b` are blocked.\n- `set` is added to the package-manager write subcommands: `mise set K=V` writes mise.toml, and `npm set` and `yarn set` write their configuration.\n\n**Allowlist (`rules/allow.json`) and always-ask flags (`rules/ask.json`).**\n- Allowed with any arguments: echo, printf, cut, tr, sort, uniq, comm, join, diff, basename, dirname, strings, date, du, df, pgrep, whoami, id, getent, printenv, `command -v|-V`.\n- Allowed as exact commands only: `env` (`env CMD` runs CMD) and the printing forms of hostname.\n- git reads:\n  - with any arguments: `ls-tree`, `rev-list`, `merge-base`, `worktree list`, `ls-remote`;\n  - remote: the bare command, `-v`, `show` and `get-url`;\n  - branch: the bare command, `--show-current`, the exact `-v`/`-vv`, and the list-mode flags followed by anything (`-a`, `-r`, `-l`, `--list`, `--contains`, `--merged`, `--points-at`, …);\n  - tag: the bare command and `-l`, `--list`, `-n<N>`, `--contains`, …;\n  - config: `--get*`, `--list*`, `-l`, `get` and `list`, also after `--global` or `--local`.\n- rtk forms of everything rtk 1.1 rewrites (`rtk rewrite` shows it): git branch and worktree, du, df, diff. A unit test checks that these stay in step.\n- `npm view`; the mise reads `--version`, `ls`, `ls-remote`, `tasks` with `ls|info|deps`, `settings` with `ls|get`, `config ls|get`. The bare `mise tasks` and `mise settings` are allowed only as exact commands.\n- Ask: `sort --compress-program` (from `--co`), `sort -T`/`--temporary-directory`, `date -s`, `git ls-remote --upload-pack/--exec`, `npm view --cache/--logs-dir`, `mise -y/--yes`.\n\n**Help layer (`src/rules.ts`, `commands.json` → `subcommandHelp`).**\n- Exact `<program> <subcommand> --help` commands for git, herdr, npm and mise (333 today), placed after `ask.json`. git, npm and mise also get their `rtk` form.\n- The list is derived from `git.write`, `git.read`, herdr's read and write paths, its `herdr <path> *` ask rules, and the per-program `subcommandHelp` lists.\n- Guarantees, each tested: no wildcard; no help rule matches an ask-listed flag; the herdr UI subcommands are left out (outside herdr nothing about them may be allowed); a form already allowed earlier is skipped, so a deny or an agent's own exact rule is never overridden; every derived command evaluates to allow.\n- The invariant \"ask flags come after every allow rule\" is relaxed for this layer only.\n- `opencode-readonly-guard rules` reports the layer.\n\n**`/guard-review` (`src/review.ts`).**\n- A prompt lists every stage of a compound command, allowed ones included, plus one general pattern per stage. A stage now counts, as a candidate and in the statistics, only if the current rules would still ask about it (not allowed, not blocked), and a candidate keeps only the general patterns that cover it.\n- On the maintainer's log, the top 50 candidates go from 341 offered \"general\" options to 48. The statistics no longer start with `echo` and `head`; they start with `sed`, `git -C`, `awk`.\n\n## Left as prompts, and why\n\n- On purpose: sed, awk, python3, node, sqlite3, ssh, rtk ssh, rtk proxy, xargs, `git -C` (needs the 2.x permission hook), `git config KEY` (globs cannot tell it from `git config KEY VALUE`), and `env CMD` / `command CMD` (they run CMD).\n- False positives of the generic rules: `cut`/`comm --output-delimiter` and `df --output` (`* --output*`), and arguments containing `-delete` (`*-delete*`).\n- Parked in TODO: git grep (`-O` runs a pager), check-ignore, show-ref, for-each-ref, hash-object, exact `<tool> --version`, absolute paths (`/usr/bin/ls`), the `2>&1` form of exact rules, `$(…)` inside arithmetic (not analyzed), `git history`/`backfill` missing from `git.write`.\n- An in-code `--help` rule for the 2.x hook is described in TODO. It cannot be `* --help` because `python3 -c CODE --help` runs CODE. It needs a per-program table of where options and the subcommand path end, and of whether the program handles `--help` there before running anything.\n\n## Checks\n\n- `mise run check`: 631 unit tests pass (was 464).\n- `mise run test:integration`: 17 pass against opencode 1.19.3.\n"
}
